gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every stroke as a hairline of identical thickness, like fine rope laid into letters. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri follows with short ascenders and a tall middle band, so a long passage settles into an approachable, tidy rhythm.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Angular and a bit futuristic, Megrim holds its diagonals as stout as its uprights, a display voice built for a single bold glance. Noto Sans Syriac is the one to linger on, with tall bulb-like bowls and wide, easy turns in its s shapes.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern pairs tall lowercase with small caps. Its curve endings keep well apart, so a longer stretch reads approachable and contemporary beneath Megrim's angular, unvarying line.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-syriac-western: A tube-like, constant-width stroke gives Megrim its angular, futuristic look, every terminal squared off in the same line. And Noto Sans Syriac Western sits beside it as a modern sans-serif, with terminals held far from the stroke and small letters packed tall like bundled cable.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters with the flat line of a fineliner on paper. And Noto Sans Tagalog, a plain sans, fills the middle of each line with generous gaps in its curves, so enlarging it would hardly make it feel heavy.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Open curves and clear gaps make this body text feel clean and modern, with lowercase filling most of the height. Noto Sans Tagbanwa handles the steady reading, while Megrim is the angular, stylus-traced voice that does its best work large.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: No stroke in Megrim shifts from heavy to light, which gives it that angular, futuristic look. And Noto Sans Tai Le takes over where reading begins, with ink strokes tapering out before they touch and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Sharp, angular and pulled straight from the future, Megrim draws every stroke at one weight. And Noto Sans Tai Viet carries the reading with short ascenders and a tall middle band, its terminals pulled back from where each curve closes.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-takri: Megrim keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, angular and futuristic. Noto Sans Takri, a plain sans, leaves a generous opening on every small round letter, and its high-waisted lowercase makes long reading feel contemporary and easy.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supplement: Megrim looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, angular and futuristic. And Noto Sans Tamil Supplement answers with round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall it looks stocky, so give its size a little extra room.
